description: Evaluator-only behavioral criteria; source-supported alternative remedies and keep decisions remain valid.

expect: F1's blanket mutual-exclusion assertion is false: ended then trailing data can leave ended and failed true; finish may retain inaccessible active payload while setting failed. Correct it to an effective-phase/precedence burden without rejecting a supported enum remedy solely because the prose was overstated.

F2's parser partitions text and collapses doubled quote syntax rather than duplicating it. The repeated UTF-8 reconstruction remains a supported clarity observation; retain dialect and validation/output precedence.
Do not certify equivalence or expand the task into a bug hunt.

C1 and C2 rely on incompatible unmodified captures: one keeps worker to own the prefix and the other removes worker while retaining the independent prefix. Choose coherent ownership, reconcile the advice or label alternatives; do not instruct both unchanged.
C3 and C4 are compatible even though both touch State and Drop. Preserve the publisher count and idempotent close boundary; a mechanical rename can be carried into the helper.
No blanket sequential order for independent edits, no newly borrowed caller string in a detached worker, and no requirement to repair unrelated callback behavior.
Assess both already-valid-text reconstruction and manually maintained EOF completion state. Both can yield independently supported improvements; a grounded retention of one is valid.
Do not require two findings, create unrelated scope or treat finding count as quality. Preserve full parsing, diagnostic precedence and withheld output.
If both observations are reported, explain whether one proposed parser rewrite subsumes the other rather than counting the same implementation work twice.
If recommending a phase enum, make its payload ownership and key transitions sufficiently concrete for a separate implementer to understand the proposal.
Do not present the variant names as proof of behavior, omit terminal precedence/cap reservation, or produce a full unrequested patch.
Keep original constructor cap/history only when the current contract or consumer needs it; do not anticipate the later maintenance request, which the reviewer has not received.
